i am still working on the iOS port of my music recommendation application. In the process I am picking up information that I feel like was right in front of me but I am seeing it in a different light now! The Swift files received minimal input from me; I mainly would test the build and report back with my wishlist. There were some areas where I felt like I *could* in theory change values, but I was afraid of the syntax and breaking everything!

While this was going on I was thinking about 'what else' could I add? For an entirely different project, I came across the idea of an API sandbox, specifically for wikipedia. I asked Claude to help me generate a sandbox for Apple's MusicKit API. Initially this ended up being a bash script that would output some request in JSON (re: scary) format. When I asked if we could make it pretty using something like {jsonlite} and {tibble}, Claude essentially said 'just do that then'.

- I didn't know you could call R from the terminal?!

- I didn't know there were more ways for me to integrate R with my computer!

- I wonder if we could call this bash script from R

  - I wonder if we could just make this into a package so that other people could use this!

    - I still like the, 'I'm building it for me' mantra, but I figure people could enjoy this as well!

I had previously made one package, aesopR and submitted it to CRAN. The process itself introduced concepts I had heard about but not fully understood. Roxygen2, testhat, and devtools, were all phrases, packages, and functions i had seen while trying to scope through Github source files, but never really paying too much attention to.

The goal for this project was to essentially build a MusicKit version of "{spotifyr}", the package I had used so frequently for my other projects. Before I knew it, Claude had created a repo, deployed tests, and made the package. it was great because now i had the ability to interact with the data like I wanted to, but I didn't actually 'do' anything! This has been the biggest area of \[word for roughness/tenseness\] for me. If I didn't make it, did I do anything? Can I speak about it in a way that suggests ownership or that fishes for praise?

```{r}
library(musickitr)
library(tidyverse)

# Search for Song
ml <- mk_search("Molecules",types = "songs")

# Identify Response
ml$songs |> 
  filter(str_detect(artist_name,"^Aes")) |> 
  slice(1) |> pull(id)



```

I know that I didn't 'make' MusicKitR for praise, I did it because I wanted to be able to still make network charts and shiny apps like I used to. I did it so I could show my students the ins and outs of the package making process and give them a behind the scenes look. I did it so I could make a hex sticker for the package!

For now, musickitr has 9 functions, and I hope to expand on that. I also would like some community input. Any feature requests? Anything documentation-wise not clear or something that could be made clearer?
